slides.title: The average professional spends 4 hours building one deck
slides.brief: Stark, deeply moody cinematic interior, shot on Leica SL2 with 35mm lens, available light only. A sprawling open-plan office at late night — most lights off, only cold blue monitor glow illuminating the space. Rows of empty desks, but at one isolated workstation sits a single figure — collared shirt, sleeves rolled up, hunched forward — surrounded by the wreckage of a presentation gone wrong: a laptop screen showing a bloated, ugly 47-slide PowerPoint deck, scattered printed slide printouts across the desk, a coffee mug tipped sideways, sticky notes covering every surface. On the monitor in the background, a clock UI reads 2:47 AM. A second monitor shows a blank slide with only a cursor blinking. The posture of the figure radiates exhaustion and quiet frustration. On the far wall behind him, in large white stencil block letters, partially lit by a single cold fluorescent tube: "THE AVERAGE PROFESSIONAL SPENDS 4 HOURS BUILDING ONE DECK." Beneath it in smaller stencil: "Most of it is guesswork. None of it is strategy." Cinematic color grade: crushed blacks, cold blue-white ambient, single desaturated amber glow from the monitor. Heavy film grain. Deep shadow vignette on all four edges.

slides.title: Every month of delay is a month they embed
slides.brief: Hyper-dramatic 3D product visualization render, Octane Render quality, studio-perfect lighting with cinematic theatrical flair. An enormous chess board fills the frame — each square rendered in polished black and deep charcoal marble, edges beveled, surface reflecting everything above it. Occupying the center squares: a single large, meticulously detailed Unilever-branded delivery truck rendered in 3D — pristine white paint, chrome bumper, clean logo on the panel, headlights on, engine visibly running (heat shimmer above the hood). Surrounding this center truck from three sides, closing in with visible tactical intent: multiple smaller competitor delivery trucks — rendered in cold grey and black, aggressive angular styling, no branding visible, uniformly threatening. Several competitor trucks have already moved into squares that are now turning grey-charcoal beneath them, "captured" squares. Two gold squares directly ahead of the Unilever truck glow warmly — still available, still open. Dominating the background of the scene: a monumental crystal hourglass, easily three times the height of the trucks, backlit by an intensely saturated red-orange gradient — sand visibly almost fully drained to the bottom chamber, only a thin trickle remaining at the neck. The hourglass casts dramatic long red shadows across the chessboard. Floating in the upper portion of the image in massive red condensed typography: "EVERY MONTH OF DELAY IS A MONTH THEY EMBED." Fine subtext beneath: "First-mover distribution advantage. Real. Durable. Nearly impossible to reverse." Dramatic rim lighting on all elements. Deep shadow vignette on frame edges.
